item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Padma writes $56=14\times 4$ and $63=21\times 3$. She asks whether that single pair of factorisations proves $56$ and $63$ have no common factor greater than $1$.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: Conclude they are co-prime from those two products alone, without checking whether another common factor was missed.
options.B: Say that calling them co-prime is what creates the incomplete factor listing, instead of testing all possible common factors.
options.C: No: one chosen factorisation of each number can miss a common factor; the search must account for every possible common factor.
options.D: Require a full prime-factorisation write-up of every integer as the only allowed method for this decision.
